executive_assessment.text: Historical station evidence distinguishes Malabo and Bata but is too sparse for national or municipality-wide climate inference.
Water coordination, meteorological capacity and forest benefit-sharing are documented governance concerns. Administrative disagreement does not establish climate-driven armed violence.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2022-06 reports: The NDC relies on only two ASECNA stations, in Malabo and Bata; cited trends show significantly rising temperatures in Malabo but a different pattern in Bata, with no significant accumulated-rainfall trend.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 8 of 8 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The UNFCCC registry lists an Equatorial Guinea NDC 3.0 submitted on 15 October 2026, but direct PDF access timed out; the 2022 NDC is historical only.
No retrieved primary source substantiates climate-driven armed conflict or violence; the 2019 water-management passage concerns conflict among resource managers.
Recent municipality-level exposure data and evidence on insecurity obstructing adaptation were not verified; the cited climate-station analysis is sparse and dated.
The retrieved water-manager disagreement is retained as a governance mediator, without labelling it armed violence or constructing an unsupported full FCV chain.
Subnational depth is limited to sparse Malabo/Bata station comparisons; comparable recent municipality-level exposure and vulnerability evidence remains a material gap.
